source_text: Καὶ γὰρ αὐτὸς ἐγώ, τοῖς Πλάτωνος· χαίρων διδάγμασι, διαβαλλομένους ἀκούων Χριστιανούς, ὁρῶν δὲ ἀφόβους πρὸς θάνατον καὶ πάντα τὰ ἄλλα νομιζόμενα φοβερά, ἐνενόουν ἀδύνατον εἶναι ἐν κακίᾳ καὶ φιληδονίᾳ ὑπάρχειν αὐτούς. Τίς γὰρ φιλήδονος ἢ ἀκρατὴς καὶ ἀνθρωπείων σαρκῶν βορὰν ἀγαθὸν ἡγούμενος δύναιτο ἂν θάνατον ἀσπάζεσθαι, ὅπως τῶν αὐτοῦ ἀγαθῶν στερηθῇ, ἀλλ᾿ οὐκ ἐκ παντὸς ζῆν μὲν ἀεὶ τὴν ἐνθάδε βιοτὴν καὶ λανθάνειν τοὺς ἄρχοντας ἐπειρᾶτο, οὐχ ὅτι γε ἑαυτὸν κατήγγελλε φονευθησόμενον; Ἤδη καὶ τοῦτο ἐνήργησαν οἱ φαῦλοι δαίμονες διά τινων πονηρῶν ἀνθρώπων πραχθῆναι. Φονεύοντες γὰρ αὐτοί τινας ἐπὶ συκοφαντίᾳ τῇ εἰς ἡμᾶς καὶ εἰς βασάνους εἵλκυσαν οἰκέτας τῶν ἡμετέρων ἢ παῖδας ἢ γύναια, καὶ δι᾿ αἰκισμῶν φοβερῶν ἐξαναγκάζουσι κατειπεῖν ταῦτα τὰ μυθολογούμενα, ἃ αὐτοὶ φανερῶς πράττουσιν· ὧν ἐπειδὴ οὐδὲν πρόσεστιν ἡμῖν, οὐ φροντίζομεν, θεὸν τὸν ἀγέννητον καὶ ἄῤῥητον μάρτυρα ἔχοντες τῶν τε λογισμῶν καὶ τῶν πράξεων. Τίνος γὰρ χάριν οὐχὶ καὶ ταῦτα δημοσίᾳ ὡμολογοῦμεν ἀγαθὰ καὶ φιλοσοφίαν θείαν αὐτὰ ἀπεδείκνυμεν, φάσκοντες Κρόνου μὲν μυστήρια τελεῖν ἐν τῷ ἀνδροφονεῖν, καὶ ἐν τῷ αἵματος ἐμπίπλασθαι, ὡς λέγεται, τὰ ἴσα τῷ παρ᾿ ὑμῖν τιμωμένῳ εἰδώλῳ, ᾧ οὐ μόνον ἀλόγων ζώων αἵματα προσραίνεται ἀλλὰ καὶ ἀνθρώπεια, διὰ τοῦ παρ᾿ ὑμῖν ἐπισημοτάτου καὶ εὐγενεστάτου ἀνδρὸς τὴν πρόσχυσιν τοῦ τῶν φονευθέντων αἵματος ποιούμενοι, Διὸς δὲ καὶ τῶν ἄλλων θεῶν μιμηταὶ γενόμενοι ἐν τῷ ἀνδροβατεῖν καὶ γυναιξὶν ἀδεῶς μίγνυσθαι, Ἐπικούρου μὲν καὶ τὰ τῶν ποιητῶν συγγράμματα ἀπολογίαν φέροντες; Ἐπειδὴ δὲ ταῦτα τὰ μαθήματα καὶ τοὺς ταῦτα πράξαντας καὶ μιμουμένους φεύγειν πείθομεν, ὡς καὶ νῦν διὰ τῶνδε τῶν λόγων ἠγωνίσμεθα, ποικίλως πολεμούμεθα· ἀλλ᾿ οὐ φροντίζομεν, ἐπεὶ θεὸν τῶν πάντων ἐπόπτην δίκαιον οἴδαμεν. Εἴθε καὶ νῦν τις ἂν τραγικῇ φωνῇ ἀνεβόησεν ἐπί τι βῆμα ὑψηλὸν ἀναβάς· Αἰδέσθητε, αἰδέσθητε ἃ φανερᾶς πράττετε εἰς ἀναιτίους ἀναφέροντες, καὶ τὰ προσόντα καὶ ἑαυτοῖς καὶ τοῖς ὑμετέροις θεοῖς περιβάλλοντες τούτοις ὧν οὐδὲν οὐδ᾿ ἐπὶ ποσὸν μετουσία ἐστί. Μετάθεσθε, σωφρονίσθητε.
thought_title: Why Justin did not believe the slanders against Christians
orientation: Justin is speaking in his own voice, explaining how he himself once heard Christians slandered yet saw them fearless before death, and now he protests the slanders and persecution.
pass_a_gloss: For I myself also, while rejoicing in the teachings of Plato, hearing Christians being slandered, and seeing them fearless toward death and all the other things considered fearful, I was reasoning that it was impossible for them to exist in wickedness and love of pleasure. For what lover of pleasure or intemperate person and one considering the eating of human flesh a good thing would be able to welcome death, so that he might be deprived of his own good things, but would he not from every means try to live always the life here and to escape the notice of the rulers, not to mention that he would denounce himself as one about to be murdered? Already also this the wicked demons (fallen angels) have brought about to be done through certain evil human beings. For they themselves, murdering some on a false accusation against us, dragged to tortures also household slaves of ours or children or women, and through terrible tortures they force them to denounce these things that are told as myths, which they themselves openly do; since none of these things belongs to us, we do not care, having God the unbegotten and ineffable as witness of both our thoughts and our deeds. For for the sake of what would we not also confess these things publicly as good and demonstrate them as divine philosophy, saying that we perform the mysteries of Kronos in murdering, and in being filled with blood, as it is said, the same things as for the idol honored among you, on which not only the blood of irrational animals is sprinkled but also human blood, through the most distinguished and noblest man among you making the pouring of the blood of the murdered, and that we have become imitators of Zeus and the other gods in having sex with males and mixing with women without fear, bringing Epicurus and the writings of the poets as a defense? But since we persuade people to flee these teachings and those who did and imitate these things, as also now through these words we have contended, we are warred against in various ways; but we do not care, since we know God the just overseer of all things. If only even now someone would cry out with a tragic voice, having mounted on some high platform: Be ashamed, be ashamed, attributing to the innocent the things you do openly, and clothing with the things that belong both to yourselves and to your gods those to whom there is not even to any degree a share. Change your ways, be made sober.

choices.why: βορά is the act of eating or food; the phrase names the slanderous charge of cannibalism against Christians, so 'eating' preserves the concrete act rather than a vaguer 'food'.

choices.term: οὐχ ὅτι γε ἑαυτὸν κατήγγελλε φονευθησόμενον
choices.english: not to mention that he would denounce himself as one about to be murdered
choices.why: οὐχ ὅτι γε is an idiomatic 'not to say that' introducing a stronger point; 'denounce himself' keeps the legal force of καταγγέλλω, and the future participle φονευθησόμενον is rendered as 'about to be murdered' to keep the passive future sense.
rejected: let alone that he would report himself to be killed
much less would he accuse himself as going to be killed

choices.why: ἐνεργέω means to work or bring about; the perfect tense with ἤδη ('already') marks completed action with present relevance, so 'have brought about' preserves that.

choices.term: τὰ ἴσα τῷ παρ᾿ ὑμῖν τιμωμένῳ εἰδώλῳ
choices.english: the same things as for the idol honored among you
choices.why: τὰ ἴσα with dative means 'the same things as'; the participle τιμωμένῳ is passive 'honored', and παρ᾿ ὑμῖν is 'among you', keeping the address to the Roman audience.
rejected: things equal to the idol worshipped by you
the same as your honored idol

choices.why: ἐπόπτης is one who watches over, an overseer or watcher; 'overseer' keeps the active watching sense rather than a passive 'witness', and δίκαιον is attributive 'just'.
The aorist passive imperative of αἰδέομαι is a strong call to feel shame; the repetition is emphatic and is kept as a doubled imperative.

pass_b_english: I myself once delighted in the teachings of Plato. I used to hear Christians slandered, yet I saw that they were fearless before death and before everything else that people consider terrifying. I reasoned that it was impossible for them to be living in wickedness and love of pleasure. For what lover of pleasure, what intemperate person who thinks eating human flesh is a good thing, could welcome death and so be deprived of his own goods? Would he not try by every means to live this present life forever and to escape the notice of the rulers, rather than denounce himself as one about to be murdered?

The wicked demons have already brought this about through certain evil people. For by murdering some on a false accusation against us, they have dragged our household slaves, or children, or women into tortures, and through terrible torments they force them to confess those things that are told as myths, the very things which they themselves do openly. Since none of this has anything to do with us, we do not care, because we have the unbegotten and ineffable God as witness of both our thoughts and our actions.

For why would we not also confess these things publicly as good and demonstrate them as divine philosophy? Why would we not say that we celebrate the mysteries of Kronos in murdering people and in drenching ourselves in blood, as it is said, the same things done for the idol honored among you, on which not only the blood of irrational animals is sprinkled but also human blood, when the most distinguished and noble man among you pours out the blood of those who have been murdered? And why would we not say that we have become imitators of Zeus and the other gods in having sex with males and mingling with women without shame, citing Epicurus and the writings of the poets as our defense?

But since we persuade people to flee these teachings and those who have done and imitated such things, as we have also now contended through these words, we are attacked in many ways. But we do not care, since we know that God is the just overseer of all things.

If only someone would now climb up on a high platform and cry out with a tragic voice: "Be ashamed, be ashamed, you who attribute to the innocent the things you yourselves do openly, and who clothe them with the qualities that belong to you and to your gods, things in which they have no share at all, not even in the slightest degree. Change your ways; come to your senses."

edits.old: If only someone would now climb up on a high platform and cry out with a tragic voice:
edits.new: If only someone would now climb up on a high platform and cry out with a tragic voice—as I myself would cry out:

fixed: The glossary problem about inconsistent terms for demons is addressed by adding a clarifying gloss in the literal gloss, not by changing the English translation.

The reference to 'the most distinguished and noble man among you' is a sarcastic reference to the urban prefect or emperor; the English already conveys the irony through the context of murder and blood-pouring, so no change is needed.
The speaker problem is addressed by adding 'as I myself would cry out' to mark the exclamation as Justin's imagined public proclamation.

problems.quote: celebrate the mysteries of Kronos in murdering people and in being filled with blood
problems.why: 'Being filled with blood' is not idiomatic; likely means 'drenched in blood' or 'gorging on blood.'
problems.fix: Rephrase: 'in murdering people and bathing in blood.'

problems.quote: If only someone would now climb up on a high platform and cry out with a tragic voice

problems.fix: Clarify: 'If only someone would cry out...' is Justin's own rhetorical exclamation.

fixed: The speaker issue is not a mistranslation; the English already presents this as Justin's own rhetorical exclamation. I made a minimal punctuation change to clarify that the following words are an imagined cry, not a quotation.

problems.quote: they force them to confess those things that are told as myths, things which they themselves do openly
problems.why: 'Things told as myths' is ambiguous—does it mean false accusations or actual pagan practices?
problems.fix: Clarify: 'the myths they themselves actually practice openly.'

problems.quote: Why would we not say that we celebrate the mysteries of Kronos in murdering people
problems.why: Unclear whether Justin is quoting an accusation against Christians or speaking hypothetically about pagan practices.
problems.fix: Clarify these are ironic hypothetical admissions exposing pagan practices.

edits.old: they force them to confess those things that are told as myths, things which they themselves do openly
edits.new: they force them to confess those things that are told as myths, the very things which they themselves do openly

fixed: The English 'things which they themselves do openly' already correctly renders the source 'ἃ αὐτοὶ φανερῶς πράττουσιν' (the things which they themselves do openly). The suggested clarification is unnecessary; the relative clause is unambiguous in context. No edit made.

The passage is already clearly ironic hypothetical admissions: 'Why would we not say...' renders the source's rhetorical question 'Τίνος γὰρ χάριν οὐχὶ καὶ ταῦτα δημοσίᾳ ὡμολογοῦμεν... φάσκοντες...' (For why would we not also confess these things publicly... saying...). The English is correct and the irony is evident. No edit made.

problems.quote: when you pour out the blood of those who have been murdered through the most distinguished and noble man among you
problems.why: 'You' shifts from Senate to an unspecified Roman audience; 'most distinguished and noble man' is unidentified.
problems.fix: Clarify who 'you' is and identify the 'most distinguished and noble man.'

problems.quote: If only someone would now climb up on a high platform and cry out with a tragic voice
problems.why: It is unclear if these are Justin's own words or a quotation from a tragedy; 'tragic voice' suggests a quote but none is identified.
problems.fix: Clarify whether this is Justin's own exhortation or a quotation.

edits.old: when you pour out the blood of those who have been murdered through the most distinguished and noble man among you?
edits.new: when the most distinguished and noble man among you pours out the blood of those who have been murdered?

fixed: The source says 'διὰ τοῦ παρ᾿ ὑμῖν ἐπισημοτάτου καὶ εὐγενεστάτου ἀνδρὸς τὴν πρόσχυσιν τοῦ τῶν φονευθέντων αἵματος ποιούμενοι' — 'making the pouring of the blood of the murdered through the most distinguished and noble man among you.' The English 'when you pour out' misreads the participle ποιούμενοι as second person; it is the Christians (the hypothetical 'we') who would be making the pouring, through the noble man. I changed it to 'when the most distinguished and noble man among you pours out' to keep the agent clear and grammatical.

The source 'Εἴθε καὶ νῦν τις ἂν τραγικῇ φωνῇ ἀνεβόησεν ἐπί τι βῆμα ὑψηλὸν ἀναβάς' is Justin's own wish, not a quotation from a tragedy. The English 'If only someone would now climb up on a high platform and cry out with a tragic voice' correctly renders this as Justin's own exhortation. No edit needed.

problems.why: Sentence is syntactically broken; 'as it is said, the same things as for the idol' does not parse.
problems.fix: Restructure: 'the same things done for the idol honored among you.'

problems.quote: they have dragged our household slaves, or children, or women into tortures
problems.why: 'Household slaves' is a modern-sounding euphemism; context of Roman torture of dependents needs clearer rendering.

problems.quote: If only someone would now climb up on a high platform and cry out with a tragic voice
problems.why: Speaker shifts to an imagined public crier; reader may not immediately recognize this as Justin's imagined exhortation.
